log: HOW MANY OF THE 1,400 ARE RIGHT -- and can we say which
calibration: 333 held-out reactions, same single-answer protocol, truth known
target:      1400 filled orphan rows, no truth and no answer key
1. THE STRATIFIER. Obscurity is defined on the TRUE catalyst, which the fill lacks. The
PREDICTED gene's literature count exists on every row -- does it track the truth's?
model predicted                n  truth obscure
an obscure gene               51         100.0%
a famous gene                282          16.3%
held-out truth-obscure share 29.1% (stratified by design)
the fill predicts an obscure gene on 1.6% of rows, so its implied truth-obscure
share is 17.6% -- against 29.1% in the benchmark. The benchmark is
HARDER than the fill on this axis, which is the opposite of what was assumed when the
obscure figure was quoted as the governing number for the whole worklist.

4. CAN WE NAME WHICH ONES? The confidence signal that separates best (0.891 against 0.456)
WAS NEVER COLLECTED for the fill -- its answers carry gene and why, nothing else. So the
question is whether the flags that do exist can substitute.
observable on every fill row                 AUC
example count                              0.532
predicted-gene literature count            0.413
full retrieval (>=12 examples)             0.562
a coin is 0.500. These are what a curator would have to triage on today.
5. THE HAND CHECK, RE-READ AGAINST GROUND TRUTH. 30 rows were verified by hand early on --
10 full-retrieval, 10 partial, 10 zero-example, which is within 4 points of the fill's own
30/37/33 split -- and scored 26/30. It was flagged at the time as NOT independent, because
the reviewer was the model that made the predictions. Held-out gives the size of that.
tier         hand check   measured     n  inflation
Self-review inflates by +0.14 overall, and the inflation is ORDERED: largest where the
examples were in front of both the predictor and the reviewer (+0.21 at full retrieval),
almost nil where there was nothing to agree with (+0.04 at zero examples). A second look
at shared evidence mostly re-endorses the first look; a second look at bare chemistry does
not. That is the mechanism, and it is why the closed-book arm withholds the examples.
READING
Point estimate 0.695 on 1367 scorable rows = about 950 correct, interval
[875, 1022]. That is an AGGREGATE. Nothing above tells a curator WHICH
950, because the one signal that separates well was never asked for. Part 3 of this
module -- an independent closed-book second opinion, calibrated on the same held-out set --
is the route to a per-row label. Run prep, then the agents, then score.
INDEPENDENT AGREEMENT -- what a second closed-book solver buys, measured not assumed
CALIBRATION on 333 held-out reactions where truth is known
the two solvers agree on              78.1%
first solver (with examples) correct  0.727
second solver (closed-book) correct   0.673
P(first answer correct | the two AGREE)      0.788   (n=260)
P(first answer correct | they DISAGREE)     0.507   (n=73)
for reference, the confidence signal that was never collected: 0.891 against 0.456 (+0.435)
bootstrap 95% CI on the gap [+0.154, +0.406]
WHERE THE SIGNAL LIVES -- it is not uniform, and that changes how it should be used
agree  disagree      gap     n
full retrieval               0.796     0.741   +0.056   140
partial or zero examples     0.782     0.370   +0.413   193
Agreement barely separates rows that already had 12 examples -- those are fine either way.
It separates the thin-retrieval rows almost completely, and those are exactly the rows the
existing flags could not touch. The two signals are complementary rather than redundant:
full retrieval alone separates by only +0.102.
ON A DISAGREEMENT, KEEP THE FIRST ANSWER -- the second is not a better answer, only a probe
first solver correct  0.507   second solver correct 0.260   (n=73)
neither correct       0.384   a disagreement usually means the reaction is hard,
not that the first answer should be swapped for the second.
APPLIED to 250 sampled fill rows
the two solvers agree on 69.6% of them
implied accuracy on the sample 0.703
scaled to all 1400 rows: about 974 agreeing rows at 0.788,
426 disagreeing at 0.507
AN UNPLANNED CONTROL. The closed-book solver was allowed to answer NONE for a reaction
with no protein catalyst. It did so on 22 of 250 fill rows, and those rows carry the mechanical
'association' flag at 22.7% against a base rate of 2.4% -- a 9x enrichment.
An independent solver with no sight of that check rediscovered part of the same class,
which is the first outside confirmation it is real. The other 17 NONEs are candidates the
mechanical check missed, and are worth reading before the check is trusted as complete.
THE LABEL. Retrieval tier and agreement, crossed, with the rate measured on held-out and
the row count projected onto all 1400 fill rows.
retrieval       second opinion      rate    share    rows
full retrieval  agrees             0.796    23.2%     325
full retrieval  disagrees          0.741     6.8%      95
thin retrieval  agrees             0.782    46.4%     650
thin retrieval  disagrees          0.370    23.6%     330
implied correct across the worklist: 960 of 1400
THE ONE CELL THAT MATTERS: thin retrieval AND the two solvers disagree.
23.6% of rows -> about 330 of 1400, at 0.370. Everything else sits near 0.78-0.80.
That is a triage rule a curator can apply in one pass, and it did not exist before.
READING
AGREEMENT IS A USABLE PER-ROW LABEL. It separates by +0.282, which is the same order
as the confidence signal that was never collected. The 974 agreeing
rows are the defensible part of the worklist at 0.788; the rest is at 0.507 and
should be treated as unreviewed. This is a label, not an average, so a curator can act on it.
